price.title: Purchase price
price.text: The price you and the seller agree on. Down payment percentages, many closing costs and the property-tax estimate are based on it.

appraisal.title: Appraised value
appraisal.text: The lender's independent estimate of what the home is worth. Loans are based on the lower of price and appraised value, so if the appraisal comes in low you cover the gap in cash or renegotiate.

rate.title: Interest rate
rate.text: Pre-filled with today's market average for each loan type. Your actual rate depends on your credit, down payment, points and lender — type the rate from your Loan Estimate to override it.

term.title: Loan term
term.text: How long you'll take to repay. A 15-year loan has a higher monthly payment but usually a lower rate and far less total interest than a 30-year loan.

credit.title: Credit score
credit.text: Sets the FHA minimum down payment (3.5% at 580+, 10% at 500–579), conventional eligibility (generally 620+) and estimated PMI pricing. Lenders may set higher minimums.

fhaLimit.title: County FHA loan limit
fhaLimit.text: The largest base loan FHA will insure in your county. Look it up and enter it to get a warning if your loan is over.

confLimit.title: Conforming loan limit
confLimit.text: Conventional loans above this are "jumbo" loans, which usually need more down and stronger credit. The {{confYear}} baseline is {{confLimit}}; high-cost counties are higher.

financeUf.title: Roll the upfront fee into the loan
financeUf.text: FHA's upfront MIP ({{ufmip}} of the base loan) and the VA funding fee can be added to the loan instead of paid in cash. You'll bring less to closing but pay a bit more each month and in interest.

vaUse.title: VA loan use
vaUse.text: With under 5% down, the funding fee is {{vaFirst}} the first time you use a VA loan and {{vaSub}} after that. Putting 5% or 10% down lowers it for both.

vaExempt.title: Funding fee exemption
vaExempt.text: Veterans receiving VA compensation for a service-connected disability, Purple Heart recipients on active duty and eligible surviving spouses don't pay the funding fee. Your Certificate of Eligibility shows it.

income.title: Gross income
income.text: Income before taxes and deductions, for everyone on the loan. Enter it per year or per month with the /yr and /mo switch; DTI always uses the monthly figure.

debts.title: Other monthly debts
debts.text: Minimum monthly payments on debts on your credit report — car and student loans, credit cards, personal loans, child support. Not utilities, phone or groceries.

points.title: Discount points
points.text: A fee paid at closing for a lower interest rate. One point is 1% of the loan. Points pay off only if you keep the loan past the break-even point the calculator shows.

ptsPer.title: Rate cut per point
ptsPer.text: How much each point lowers your rate. About 0.25% is common, but it varies by lender and day — use the figure from your Loan Estimate.

tbType.title: Temporary buydown
tbType.text: Lowers your rate for the first 1–3 years, then it steps up to the full rate. Usually paid upfront by the seller or builder. Lenders still qualify you at the full rate.

downAmt.title: Down payment
downAmt.text: Cash you put toward the price. Minimums: FHA 3.5% (580+ credit), VA 0%, conventional 3–5%. With 20% down, conventional loans have no PMI. Assistance can cover some or all of it.

dpaState.title: Down payment assistance
dpaState.text: State and local programs that help with the down payment or closing costs. Pick where you're buying to see them, and check each program's income, price and first-time-buyer rules.

dpaType.title: Assistance types
dpaType.text: Grant: never repaid. Forgivable: a loan that's forgiven if you stay a set number of years. Deferred: a 0% loan with no payments, repaid when you sell or refinance. Repayable: a second loan with a monthly payment.

closing.title: Closing costs
closing.text: Fees to get the loan and transfer the home: lender, appraisal, title, recording, prepaid interest, insurance and escrow. Buyers often pay 2–5% of the price. Your Loan Estimate lists them.

credits.title: Seller / lender credits
credits.text: Money the seller or lender puts toward your closing costs. Credits can't exceed your costs or be taken as cash, and seller help is capped: {{capText}}

payoff.title: Seller's mortgage payoff
payoff.text: What the seller still owes on their mortgage. Used only to estimate the seller's net proceeds.

tax.title: Property tax
tax.text: Set by your county and city. Use the current bill or the rate from the county tax office; taxes are often reassessed after a sale.

ins.title: Homeowners insurance
ins.text: Lenders require it. Get a quote for this home — premiums vary a lot by location, age and coverage.

hoa.title: HOA dues
hoa.text: Monthly homeowners association fees, if the property has one. Lenders count them in your housing payment.

mip.title: FHA annual MIP
mip.text: FHA's monthly mortgage insurance. For this loan: {{fhaMip}} a year, {{fhaMipDur}}.

pmi.title: PMI
pmi.text: Private mortgage insurance on conventional loans with under 20% down. Priced by credit score and down payment; it ends automatically at 78% loan-to-value, and you can usually ask to remove it at 80%.

ltv.title: Loan-to-value (LTV)
ltv.text: Your loan divided by the home's value. A lower LTV means less risk for the lender and often better pricing and less mortgage insurance.

dti.title: Debt-to-income (DTI)
dti.text: Front-end: housing payment ÷ gross monthly income. Back-end: housing plus other debts ÷ gross monthly income. Lenders use it to judge what you can afford.

cash.title: Cash to close
cash.text: What you bring to closing: down payment plus closing costs, minus credits and assistance. Earnest money you already paid counts toward it.

compare.title: Compare loan types
compare.text: Runs the same home through FHA, VA and conventional rules side by side. Green marks the lowest in each row. VA loans require military service eligibility.

party.title: Buyer & seller costs
party.text: Who pays which closing costs. Customs vary by state and everything is negotiable; buyer costs the seller pays count toward the seller-concession cap.
